exclusions.B: He had climbed into the roof with a lamp that morning: the rafters were sound, the gale had taken only the sheeting, and the members could repair it themselves for the price of a summer's teas.
exclusions.C: The vote was eleven to two for Pryor's plan.
exclusions.D: Tobias Fenn, the groundsman, remarked that forty pounds would pay for moving the scoreboard to higher ground.
exclusions.E: Then the captain, Neil Pryor, took a stand.

WV8-P01.4.note: Pryor 'took a stand' by declaring a position against selling, which he then argues, so the word means a stance; no physical seating, stall or grove is involved.

exclusions.A: Anyone who sits on its veranda on a match day is sitting under the work of a village that looked hard at its own building, trusted what it found, and was proved right.
exclusions.B: The building, members told one another, had survived worse.
exclusions.D: The roof those members nailed down is still on the pavilion, sixty years and many gales later.
exclusions.E: By June the roof was whole again, on the same building and the same footings, a few yards from the same river.

WV8-P01.5.note: The closing paragraph praises the village for looking hard, trusting what it found and being proved right, which is admiration, not detachment, criticism, amusement or longing.

exclusions.A: He raised nine hundred dollars in Wendle for buckets and waders, and on the first morning forty volunteers waded in behind him to carry mussels from the shrinking shallows to the channel.
exclusions.C: Odile Prask, who runs the breeding hatchery at Sallow Ford, took two hundred mussels into her tanks as a reserve.
exclusions.D: Teo had sketched a wall of sandbags across the cove's mouth, but there was money for one plan, and Kettle's was already moving.
exclusions.E: Teo had sketched a wall of sandbags across the cove's mouth, but there was money for one plan, and Kettle's was already moving.

WV8-P02.4.note: Kettle raised money in the town for buckets and waders, i.e. collected funds; nothing was mentioned, reared, built, or increased from an existing sum.

exclusions.A: In the channel, nine in ten of her tagged mussels came through the winter.
exclusions.B: By the fourth evening the volunteers had moved more than three thousand.
exclusions.C: Her report lists every volunteer by name, which seems the least such an effort has earned.
exclusions.E: What stands out in Marrow's notes is the arithmetic of the rescue: forty people, four days, three thousand mussels, each one lifted by hand.

WV8-P02.5.note: The author stresses the hand-carried scale of the rescue and says naming every volunteer is 'the least such an effort has earned', an admiring judgment on a plan the passage shows succeeding.
